name: iiif.archive.org
aliases: iiif.archive.org (free IIIF Image API over any uploaded image)

card.provider: iiif.archive.org (free IIIF Image API over any uploaded image)
card.summary: No separate quota. It is a free image server over items you already hold, one image per item. Capacity therefore follows the 1TB/item rule.

record.provider: iiif.archive.org (free IIIF Image API over any uploaded image)

free_tier.stated: No separate quota. It is a free image server over items you already hold, one image per item. Capacity therefore follows the 1TB/item rule.

retention.stated: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.

egress.terms: Free, and it is a rendering endpoint, so one stored master serves arbitrary region/size/rotation/quality requests. The cheapest possible way to serve image bytes at many sizes.

record.tooling: IIIF Image API v2 and v3 (Cantaloupe server); any IIIF viewer or plain GET on /iiif/<identifier>/info.json; no rclone backend
record.chaining: Allows storing high-resolution master images and serving rendered image tiles or thumbnails via IIIF endpoints, reducing outbound transfer bandwidth across requests.
record.limits_note: One image per item for reliable IIIF (multiple images need multiple items); must upload to the 'Community Image' collection or the viewer breaks; test-style uploads can be deleted after 30 days.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence
